open_points.subject: A1 subfolder traversal
open_points.text: A subfolder the listing showed that is no longer that folder when it is opened, because it became a link or another object, is not entered; one that cannot be opened is refused as a subfolder that cannot be listed.
open_points.question: When a listed subfolder is replaced by a link or non-folder before opening, is the entry merely skipped or is the whole scan refused with `folder_unavailable`?
options: Skip the replaced entry and continue the scan
Refuse the whole scan with `folder_unavailable`

witness.initial: A scan has listed subfolder `day1`, which contains a photo.
events: Syncthing replaces `day1` with a symbolic link after the listing and before the deliverer opens it.
The deliverer attempts to continue the scan.
outcomes: The deliverer does not enter `day1` and returns a complete scan without that photo.
The deliverer refuses the whole scan with `folder_unavailable`.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees either a successful partial-looking scan or a refusal.

open_points.subject: A1 folder replacement identity
open_points.text: A subfolder the listing showed that is no longer that folder when it is opened, because it became a link or another object, is not entered
open_points.question: How must the implementation detect that a subfolder was replaced by another ordinary directory between listing and opening, and what happens when it detects that replacement?
options: Compare directory identity from the listing with the opened directory and skip it
Compare directory identity and refuse the scan
Open any ordinary directory now present under that name
open_points.default_guess: Open descriptor-relative without following links and accept the ordinary directory present when it is opened, because no required identity value or comparison is defined.

events: Another actor renames `day1` away and installs a different ordinary directory under the same name.
outcomes: The replacement is treated as another object and is not entered.
The successfully opened replacement directory is scanned.
witness.observer: The caller sees different files in the scan result.

open_points.subject: A2 transparent-pixel conversion
open_points.text: The pixels are converted to RGB as decoded, without colour management. Transparent areas become white.
open_points.question: Is alpha composited onto white before RGB conversion, or may RGB conversion discard alpha before the white composition is applied?
options: Composite decoded colour and alpha onto white, then produce RGB
Convert to RGB first using the decoder's alpha-discard behaviour
Require a particular premultiplied-alpha conversion
open_points.default_guess: Composite onto white in a colour-plus-alpha representation and then convert the result to RGB.

witness.initial: A PNG contains fully transparent pixels whose stored RGB components are black.
events: The image is decoded and re-encoded as JPEG.
outcomes: The transparent area is white in the stored JPEG.
Alpha is discarded during RGB conversion and the area is black in the stored JPEG.
witness.observer: The owner and client see different stored pixels.

open_points.subject: A2 JPEG encoding
open_points.text: baseline, not progressive, three colour channels with the colour resolution halved in both directions (4:2:0), the imported `PHOTO_QUALITY` constant as its quality, and no colour profile and no metadata
open_points.question: Which quantisation tables, quality-to-table mapping, DCT/rounding behaviour, chroma siting, Huffman-table strategy and other encoder choices define the stored JPEG bytes?
options: Adopt the selected image library's defaults
Specify an exact encoder and all byte-affecting settings
Require only the listed properties and allow different JPEG byte streams
open_points.default_guess: Use the selected image library's baseline 4:2:0 encoder with quality 85 and otherwise its documented defaults.

witness.initial: One valid source image is delivered by two conforming implementations using different JPEG encoders.
events: Each encoder uses baseline JPEG, 4:2:0 and quality 85 with no metadata.
Each placement records the output length and SHA-256.
outcomes: One valid JPEG byte stream, size and SHA-256 are stored.
A different valid JPEG byte stream, size and SHA-256 are stored.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees different `size` and `sha256`, and the Portal stores different bytes.

open_points.subject: A2 image reduction
open_points.text: the longest side is reduced to the limit when it is larger
open_points.question: How are the other dimension, fractional target dimensions, resampling filter, edge handling and rounding decided?
options: Preserve aspect ratio and round dimensions down with a specified filter
Preserve aspect ratio and round to nearest with a specified filter
Use the image library's resize defaults
open_points.default_guess: Preserve aspect ratio, round the calculated secondary dimension to the nearest integer, and use a high-quality library resampler.

witness.initial: A source has dimensions whose aspect-preserving secondary dimension is fractional at the maximum side.
events: The implementation reduces its longest side.
outcomes: The secondary dimension is rounded down and one resampled pixel grid is stored.
The secondary dimension is rounded to nearest and a different pixel grid is stored.
witness.observer: The owner sees potentially different pixels, and the placement has different size and SHA-256.

open_points.subject: A5 token-file startup
open_points.text: At the start the file is decoded as UTF-8, a byte sequence that is not UTF-8 ending the start, and the Unicode whitespace at both ends is removed. The service does not start when the group or others have any permission on the file, or when what remains has fewer than 32 characters or any character that is not visible ASCII (`!` to `~`)
open_points.question: What must happen when the token-file path is absent, cannot be opened or read, is a directory, or is a symbolic link, and which exact Unicode whitespace set is stripped?
options: End startup for every open/read/type failure and use the runtime's Unicode whitespace definition
End startup and define an explicit accepted file type and whitespace code-point set
Permit links and other readable objects and use implementation defaults
open_points.default_guess: Require a readable regular file, reject links and other file types, end startup on every access failure, and use the language runtime's Unicode whitespace definition.

open_points.subject: A6 unsafe-reference precedence
open_points.text: otherwise the delivery is refused with `unsafe_reference`
open_points.question: At what point in A3 rule 4's check order is the binary-store containment check made, especially when an existing placement already exists?
options: Check before taking the project lock
Check inside the lock before checking an existing placement
Check only when a new stored image is about to be written
Check existing placements too and let `unsafe_reference` override replay
open_points.default_guess: Check it inside the project lock only when a new image is about to be written; an existing placement replays first.

witness.initial: A placement record already exists, and a binary-store folder is now a link leading outside the store.
events: The caller repeats delivery of the placed source.
outcomes: A3 rule 2 wins and the call answers `replayed`.
A6 rule 1 wins and the call is refused with `unsafe_reference`.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a replay or a refusal.

open_points.subject: A6 binary-store containment
open_points.text: its path, resolved with the links of the binary store, must lie below the resolved store, otherwise the delivery is refused with `unsafe_reference`
open_points.question: How is containment preserved if a store directory is replaced by a link after resolution but before the temporary file or final file is opened?
options: Use descriptor-relative, no-follow opens for every store component
Resolve again immediately before each open and rename
Permit the race because only the resolved pre-check is required
open_points.default_guess: Open every store component descriptor-relative without following links and refuse with `unsafe_reference` if any component changes incompatibly.

witness.initial: The checked destination lies below the binary store and its project directory is ordinary.
events: The deliverer completes the resolution check.
Another actor replaces the project directory with a link to an outside directory.
The deliverer creates and renames the image.
outcomes: The image is written outside the binary store.
The no-follow open fails and the delivery is refused with `unsafe_reference`.
witness.observer: The server operator sees an outside write, while the caller sees success or refusal.

open_points.subject: A6 retry after directory-sync failure
open_points.text: a failure to synchronise the folder after it is a failed write of that operation, while the renamed file stays and a repeated call finds it (A3 rule 2, A4)
open_points.question: With a renamed image but no placement record after the failed operation, does the repeated delivery reuse that image, overwrite it, or treat it as an existing placement?
options: Reuse the existing image and then write the placement record
Write the image again as A3 rule 5 states
Answer `replayed` despite the absent placement record
open_points.default_guess: Rewrite the image atomically and then create the placement record; an image without a record is not a placement.

open_points.subject: M04 name and A3 scan independence
open_points.text: `name` is the name M02 gave the source when it was placed
open_points.question: What name is stored when a caller delivers a valid file without first performing a scan, which A3 expressly permits because the service keeps no memory of scans?
options: Store the request's validated `name`
Require a prior M02 observation
Construct an M02-equivalent name during delivery
open_points.default_guess: Store the validated `name` supplied in the delivery request.

witness.initial: A valid unplaced photo exists and no scan has been performed.
events: The authenticated caller directly requests delivery with the photo's valid relative name and source id.
outcomes: A3 permits placement and M04 stores the request name.
M04 cannot obtain a name that M02 gave, so delivery must be refused or an unstated observation must be created.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees successful delivery or refusal.

open_points.subject: INV-01
open_points.text: INV-01: after a scan, a placement, a repeated placement and a mark, the source folder holds the same files with the same bytes, modification times and modes (`test_no_operation_changes_the_source_folder`).
open_points.question: What must the test show about source directories, names, ownership, links and other metadata to prove that no operation creates, changes, moves or deletes anything, rather than only that listed file bytes, modification times and modes are unchanged?
options: Assert an exact before/after tree including directories, entry types and all protected metadata
Narrow INV-01 to files, bytes, modification times and modes
Declare which incidental filesystem metadata, such as access time, may change
open_points.default_guess: Narrow the invariant to deliberate changes of directory entries, file bytes, modification times and modes, and test the complete tree for those properties.

open_points.subject: INV-02
open_points.text: INV-02: for content with no placement, an empty or absolute name, a name with an empty, `.` or `..` segment, an ignored name at any level, a folder, and a path through a symbolic link each fail with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure and add no file except the project lock (`test_a_name_a_scan_would_not_report_is_not_delivered`).
open_points.question: How does this test prove the invariant that delivery opens no path failing condition 1, and what must it show for absent segments, folder-open failures, metadata-read failures and replacements occurring between checks and opens?
options: Instrument filesystem opens and assert that no final source file is opened in every condition-1 branch
Interpret INV-02 as permitting folder opens needed to decide condition 1 but forbidding opening the last segment for reading
Replace the invariant with the currently tested outcome-and-no-write property
open_points.default_guess: Clarify that validation may open folders but must not open the last segment for reading after condition 1 fails, and assert opens as well as outcomes for every branch.

open_points.subject: INV-06
open_points.text: INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged, with one placement record in place (`test_a_repeated_placement_writes_no_durable_state`).
open_points.question: Does proving that final durable contents are unchanged suffice for “a repeated placement writes nothing,” or must the test show that no temporary file, rewrite, rename, synchronisation or record write is attempted?
options: Instrument all store and state write operations and assert zero writes
Redefine the invariant as no durable-state change
Treat identical rewrites as allowed
open_points.default_guess: Instrument the storage ports and assert zero write attempts after the existing placement is found.

open_points.subject: INV-19
open_points.text: INV-19: delivering content that has no placement under the name of a conflict copy fails with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure, adds no file except the project lock and changes no existing file (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`).
open_points.question: How must the Required test demonstrate that the conflict copy was never read, rather than merely showing the same refusal and final filesystem state after it was read?
options: Instrument source-file opens and reads and assert zero byte reads
Change the invariant to only require refusal and no durable change
Rely on check order without a witness assertion
open_points.default_guess: Instrument the source access port and assert that the conflict-copy file is never opened for reading.

open_points.subject: INV-20
open_points.text: and a record that is a link, dangling or not, or that names another source is refused the same way (`test_a_record_not_written_at_its_address_is_refused`).
open_points.question: What Required test shows the normative case of a record naming another project, and what assertion proves that a damaged record creates neither a stored image nor any new placement or mark?
options: Add wrong-project cases and assert the entire binary/state stores are unchanged
Treat “damaged record” in the earlier sentence as implicitly covering all these cases
Narrow the normative validation rule to the cases explicitly named by the test
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit wrong-project placement and mark records and assert no stored image, placement or mark is created.

open_points.subject: INV-13
open_points.text: INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
open_points.question: What must be shown for marks refused before the clock point, refused after it, replayed, and refused while acquiring the project lock, so that the test covers the reading rules for every mark outcome?
options: Test zero reads for each pre-clock refusal and exactly one for each post-clock refusal and replay
Treat one successful mark as sufficient evidence for all mark paths
Narrow INV-13 to successful marks
open_points.default_guess: Add branch tests proving zero reads before the specified point and exactly one read for successful, replayed and post-clock-refused marks.

open_points.subject: A2 configured time zone
open_points.text:
otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`.
open_points.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: The passage must name the `timezone` field of the settings object, rather than referring only to “the configured time zone”.
